title: Beam diagram creator
summary: Build a straight beam with pinned and fixed supports, point forces, couples and distributed loads; see reactions, shear force, bending moment and deflection solved in the browser by the stiffness method, including statically indeterminate beams, and download the same model as an MSC Nastran SOL 101 bulk data deck.

units.internal: SI: m, N, N/m, N·m, Pa, m², m⁴

conventions: x runs along the beam from its left end; +y is up.
Point forces and distributed loads are positive upward: enter downward loads as negative numbers.
Couples, rotations and support moments are positive counter-clockwise.
Shear V(x) is the sum of the upward forces to the left of the section.
Bending moment M(x) is positive when it sags the beam (tension on the bottom fibre); dM/dx = V and dV/dx = q.
At a point force V jumps by the force; at a couple C, M jumps by −C. Both one-sided values are reported.
assumptions: Linear elastic, small displacement, static loading.
Euler–Bernoulli bending: plane sections stay plane and shear deformation is neglected.
Uniform prismatic section and one material along the whole beam.
Loads act in the plane of bending through the shear centre; no axial load, torsion, temperature or dynamics.
A pin restrains deflection; a fixed support restrains deflection and slope. Supports are rigid.
method: Direct stiffness method with two-node Hermite beam elements between the supports and the beam ends. Point forces, couples and distributed loads inside each element enter as consistent nodal loads, which are the exact fixed-end actions for Euler–Bernoulli beams, so nodal deflections and reactions are exact and statically indeterminate supports need no special handling. Load points stay out of the stiffness matrix, so closely spaced loads do not degrade its conditioning, and there is no cap on the number of supports or loads. Shear and moment are then recovered exactly by statics from the loads and reactions, and deflection between nodes by integrating M/EI. Results are checked against an independent exact-arithmetic Python solver (Macaulay integration with compatibility conditions) on shared fixtures.

presets.label: Pinned–pinned, uniform load
presets.note: Statically determinate: reactions from equilibrium alone.

presets.label: Fixed–fixed, uniform load
presets.note: Indeterminate to degree 2: end moments wL²/12 hog, mid-span wL²/24 sags.

presets.label: Fixed–fixed, off-centre point load
presets.note: End moments Pab²/L² and Pa²b/L² are unequal, so the reactions are too.

presets.label: Pinned–pinned, point load and couple
presets.note: The couple makes the moment diagram jump; the point load makes the shear jump.

presets.label: Propped cantilever (fixed–pinned)
presets.note: Indeterminate to degree 1: the prop carries 3wL/8.

presets.label: Cantilever, tip load
presets.note: Statically determinate: the whole load returns through the fixed end.

presets.label: Two-span continuous beam
presets.note: Indeterminate to degree 1: the middle support carries 5wL/4 and hogs by wL²/8.

nastran.dialect: MSC Nastran, SOL 101 linear statics, large-field fixed-format bulk data

cards.use: One grid per node along basic X; PS=345 permanently removes out-of-plane translation and rotations.
One bar per element, orientation vector X1,X2,X3 = 0,1,0 (element y = basic +Y).
A, I1 (in-plane I), I2, J; K1/K2 blank = zero shear flexibility, matching Euler–Bernoulli.
E and ν; G left blank so NASTRAN derives it.
Set 1: pin = components 12, fixed = 126 at the support grid.
Load set 2: point forces along basic Y and couples about basic Z at grids.
Load set 2: TYPE=FY, SCALE=FR from 0 to 1 on each element under a distributed load, with the intensities at its ends.
Asks MSC Nastran to write the Patran results database (.xdb) alongside the run.

run: Save the deck, e.g. beam.bdf, on a machine with a licensed MSC Nastran installation.
PARAM,POST,0 makes the run write beam.xdb next to beam.f06; open it in Patran (or another .xdb reader) to post-process.
Compare DISPLACEMENT T2 (deflection, m) and R3 (slope, rad), and SPCFORCES T2 (reaction, N) and R3 (support moment, N·m), with this page. These are in basic coordinates and use the same signs.
nastran.status: The deck is generated from the same model the page solves and is checked by reading it back and re-solving it with the independent Python reference. This page does not run NASTRAN and does not produce an .xdb file itself.
